## Similarity of Muscle Activities

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](figures/fig2-emg.png){height="820"}
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
1.2 m/s level walking, 8 muscles vs. EMG (22 people)

**Synergistic** → within the human range for **all 8**

**Independent** → outside it for **5 / 8**; GAS, ST, BF negatively correlated
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
For the independent controller, five of the eight muscles fall outside the range of correlations you see between humans, and GAS, ST, and BF are actually negatively correlated with the EMG.

The synergistic controller is within the human range for all eight. The plantarflexors agree in both timing and magnitude. ST, BF, and RF have lower correlations, but the paper points out those muscles also have the broadest variability between people.

One thing worth noting from the figure: for TA and RF, the independent controller's median correlation is actually higher than the synergistic one, even though both are within the human range.


imilarity between predicted muscle activations and experimental EMG envelopes across eight lower-limb
muscles. Top box plots show Pearson correlation coefficients between predicted muscle activations and experimental
EMG envelopes during level treadmill walking at 1.2 m/s for soleus (SOL), gastrocnemius medialis (GAS), tibialis
anterior (TA), semitendinosus (ST), biceps femoris (BF), rectus femoris (RF), vastus medialis (VM), and vastus
lateralis (VL). Gray box plots represent the cross-human experimental benchmark derived from 22 participants of the
open-source dataset, and the surrounding gray shaded regions indicate the corresponding envelope of cross-human
variability. Orange and blue box plots correspond to independent and synergistic control conditions, respectively. Round
dots denote individual correlation coefficients (n = 231 for cross-human pairwise comparisons; n = 22 per controller
for correlations between simulated and experimental activations). Bottom line plots show representative activation
profiles over the normalized gait cycle, where gray curves indicate experimental EMG envelopes across participants,
and colored curves represent predicted activations from the independent (orange) and synergistic (blue) controllers.
Muscle activations were normalized to reference voluntary contraction (RVC): for each muscle, predicted activations
were scaled to the maximum amplitude observed within each controller, whereas experimental EMG envelopes were
normalized to the subject-specific maximum amplitude.
:::
